openIssues: **Nights are unreadable, and rainy nights are pure black.** game_night.png (March, 23:00, rain) averages RGB [15,18,24] over the play area: terrain, river and field edges are all gone. Even the clear full-moon showcase night averages [25,34,39] (preset_night.png) and the paths barely read. The cause is that the ambient floor `[32,40,76]` in `sky.js ambientFor` sits *below* the brief's ≈[38,48,92], and then `fx.drawScreen` stacks more darkening on top of the multiply: a soft-light blue wash at 0.55·night, 0.28·night desaturation, and a vignette of up to 0.62 (0.2+0.28 night+0.08 rain). Fix it like this: the floor must hold *after* the grade, so move the floor up to about the brief's [38,48,92] for the new-moon/rain worst case. Cap the night vignette at about 0.35. Stop the night soft-light wash from darkening (use a lighten-safe tint, or apply it only to the ambient colour). Aim for a rainy new-moon night where fields, paths and the river silhouette stay legible at a glance (mean luminance of roughly 35–45 on grass).

**The golden-hour grade is muddy, not golden.** preset_golden.png and golden_1930.png: the whole field goes olive/khaki and the reds go brown. The amber ambient multiply plus the orange `soft-light` gradient on green gives mud. Golden hour needs warm, *saturated* highlights on the sunlit side and relatively cooler shadows. Reduce the multiply amber at 3–12° elevation (for example keep G ≥ 0.85·R), replace the soft-light orange with a lower-alpha `overlay`/`screen` warm tint that lifts rather than dirties, and do not apply the overcast desaturation when `golden > 0`.

**Fog (and the fog component of snow) reads as a stretched-noise overlay.** preset_fog.png, fog_0700.png, snow_1230.png: strong vertical column streaks run across the whole screen. They come from the anisotropic pattern stretch (`tile(... ang, 2.2 / 1.6)`) aligned with the wind, which here is roughly N–S. On top of that, the veil plus two bank layers wash out about 70% of the contrast (the fence and wall almost vanish in fog_0700). Drop the stretch to ≤1.3 or rotate the two layers by different angles so they don't reinforce each other. Soften the bank edges (the `smooth(lo,hi)` window is too narrow at 160 px per 150 m). Cap the combined fog opacity so gameplay objects keep about 50% contrast. Bank placement should also vary with some low-frequency depth, not tile uniformly.

**The `closeup` preset is not "at dusk" as the README claims.** preset_closeup.png at 21:50 in July is full night (mean [42,49,45]), and the lamp pools read sickly yellow-green. Either move it to about 20:45 so the lamp shows against blue-hour light, or rename it. A showcase preset has to demonstrate what it claims.

**CAP / short-lease exploit (confirmed).** In the showcase valley I rented every `forRent`/`forSale` parcel (15.1 ha) on the day before CAP day (doy 27) and ended every lease the next morning. That paid €229 of rent and received €3,548 of CAP for those hectares, a net **+€3,828 for one day**, repeatable every year.
`rentParcel` charges nothing up front.
`endLease` works at any moment with no notice or minimum term.
CAP pays on `farmedHa()` measured on a single day (`land.js` `landDay`).
Pay CAP pro rata for the days each parcel was held in the last 36 days, or only on parcels held since before sowing season.
Give leases a minimum term (e.g. 1 game year, or until after the next harvest).
Make `endLease` early cost the rest of the term or a notice penalty.
Charge rent monthly in advance.
**Progression curve: growing the farm does not pay, and buying land never does.** My measured figures, all per game year:

**Land.** The rent/price ratio is about 1% (e.g. Lindeveld is €57.4k/ha to buy and €566/ha/yr to rent). Buying adds 11.5% duty, never appreciates and resells at 95%. With loans at 4.5%, a mortgaged parcel loses money every year compared with renting it. Owning land exists only to raise the credit limit.

**Area.** Contractor-farmed rented wheat makes about €150/ha. With unlimited cash and storage, 20 ha gives mean +€2.9k and 50 ha gives +€1.0k. At 50 ha the per-lot saturation (wheat depth 80 t per point) takes most of the margin, and yearly swings reach −€40k/+€52k.
**Jobs.** A greedy player who accepts every offer earns **€23.2k/yr** from 84 jobs. Farming 5 ha earns under €1k.

**Time to buy.** One game year is 14.4 real hours. The cheapest parcel for sale (Bergske, €131k + duty ≈ €146k) takes about 6–15 game years of typical cash flow, which is 90–220 real hours. The compact combine (€145k) pays back through €165/ha harvest jobs in 20+ years.
Set a target progression, e.g. "first owned parcel by year 3–4, second tractor by year 2, combine by year 5".
Tune to that target, for example:

**Panels overlap the bottom-centre prompt at the target resolution.** `.hv-panel { max-height: calc(100vh - 118px - 150px) }` lets the sheet end at about y=782, while the prompt sits at y≈745–785. In market_1230.png / market_1930.png the "E — Hoe the verge" prompt is hidden under the Market sheet, and in finances_1230.png it pokes out underneath. Compute the max height from the actual top of the bottom-centre slot (or hide/raise the prompt while a panel is open) so that nothing is covered at 1600×900.

**1024×700 layout collides.** narrow_jobs.png, narrow_finances.png and narrow_land.png show the 700 px sheet covering the minimap's "Harvest Valley" caption and cutting the toast stack in half ("…nned on the jobs board."). Toasts must never sit under a panel. Either put `.hv-toasts` above `.hv-panelwrap` in z-order and move it clear, or clamp the panel width to the space between the side columns (`min(700px, 100vw - 2×(minimap width + gutter))`) and shift toasts below the panel's right edge. The README's own threshold of "< 1000 px" is not met at 1024.

**An invisible dead zone above the toolbar eats world clicks.** The `ui:toolbar` HUD node is `hv-hit`, 348×91 px, and includes the tool-name row plus the gap. Probes at (746,807) and (631,800), on transparent pixels beside the "Hoe" chip, returned `uiCapturing=true` and the canvas never received the click. Give the bare wrappers (`card:false` HUDs, `toolsWrap`) `pointer-events:none` and only mark the visible card, chip and prompt as `.hv-hit`.

**Declare the optional dependencies.** `manifest.optionalDeps: []`, but the module reads `simulation`, `environment` (via world), `terrain` and `roads` through `ctx.modules.get`. The brief lists them as the data sources and ARCHITECTURE §1 expects them in the manifest (boot also uses optionalDeps for init order). Set `optionalDeps: ['simulation','environment','terrain','roads']`. This is harmless to wave-1 isolation because they stay optional.
**Main-thread synthesis per one-shot (perf budget).** `grainBuffer()` (synth.js) is called inside `grains()` on every `play()`:
footstep-* costs 3.8–14 ms per step, thunder 11 ms and harvest-thresh 58 ms (measured in Chrome).
One walking character at about 2 steps/s already burns about 10 ms/s. A combine harvesting would stall a frame on every call.

Fix: pre-bake N (e.g. 4–6) seeded variants per grain recipe with `cachedBuffer()` and pick one per call, varying playbackRate, offset and filter. Do this lazily on first use of each id, or amortised in idle slices after unlock.
Target: every `play()` under 0.5 ms main-thread time.

**Loop first-creation hitches.** The first `rain` takes 157 ms, `river` 99 ms, `crickets` 52 ms and `wind` 47 ms. Together with `resources()` (46 ms) this lands in one frame, either on the first gesture (the director immediately creates wind and birds) or when weather or night first arrives.
Generate these buffers in time-sliced chunks after unlock (a few ms per frame) and only start a layer once its buffer is ready.
Or at least generate them before the director needs them, not synchronously inside `director()`.

**Director must use environment's eased weather, not the discrete `kind`.** `world.environment.weather` publishes smoothly ramped `rain`, `storm`, `snow`, `fog` and `precipitation` (0..1). `readWeather()` instead derives `rain` from `kind==='rain'|'storm'` and `intensity`, with three consequences:
Rain audio snaps on and off at the kind boundary while the visuals crossfade.
`intensity || 0.6` turns a legitimate 0 intensity into 0.6.
`snow` and the storm thunder are boolean, so the muffle jumps from 18 kHz to 2.8 kHz in one step, and thunder is gated on `kind==='storm'` instead of `weather.storm > x`.

**The ambience boards contradict themselves.** In ambience-day_0700.png the sidebar says "07:00" but the big "What you hear now" panel says "director mix at 05:10". Likewise, the ambience-night 07:00 and 12:30 shots still show the 23:30 owl/cricket mix. The board is rendered once at stage time and never follows the clock.
Either re-render the mix when the clock or weather changes by more than a threshold, or label it explicitly as the preset snapshot.
The offline mix also omits the fog/snow muffle: amb-night-snow.png shows full energy up to 10 kHz in snow, which misrepresents what the game plays. Route the offline mix through `muffleCutoff(W)`.
